title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Arcade Score Screen. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Arcade Score Screen
options.thesis: The queue as an intense, neon-lit digital scoreboard where your number is your name.
options.viewport: A stark black screen with glowing neon typography, blinking cursors, and raw numbers.
options.risk: Can feel too playful for a serious clinic environment.

raised.raise: Unapologetic use of vivid, clashing accent colors to draw the eye to the active state.

options.label: The Deli Ticket Snail
options.thesis: Visceral, nostalgic proof of a physical queue, modernized.
options.viewport: A bright red mechanical container aesthetic dispensing a stark, high-contrast thermal ticket.
options.risk: Also the direction most runs in this category land on.

options.label: Seven-Segment Totem
options.thesis: The queue as an undeniable, rigid mask of unlit and lit LED segments.
options.viewport: Massive red segments against black, scaling as whole units, instant segment swaps.
options.case: Fuses perfectly: queues are literally numbers; highly trusted utility form.
options.risk: Can read too stark or aggressive if the ghost cells are too dim.

options.label: Cassette Futurist Fascia
options.thesis: The dashboard as physical switches and amber LED progress ladders.
options.viewport: Strict panel grid with engraved labels, chrome toggles snapping into state.
options.case: Physical switches and progress ladders map well to taking a ticket and waiting.
options.risk: Skeuomorphism can alienate users used to flat UI.

options.label: Madrid Scene Cover
options.case: Fuses poorly: queues need order, not scattered, misregistered noise.
options.kept: Vivid accent colors for the active state.

canonCard.label: The Apple-esque Utility
canonCard.thesis: What this category ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor expects: bento boxes, subtle borders, high contrast.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design. Too 'AI-coded'.
